title: IF THEY WILL NOT LISTEN, WHY WOULD HE?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go, tell Pharaoh king of Egypt to let the Israelites go out of his country." But Moses said to the Lord, "If the Israelites will not listen to me, why would Pharaoh listen to me, since I speak with faltering lips?"" - Exodus 6:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses' logic sounds reasonable. If my own people, who have everything to gain, will not listen to me, why on earth would the king of Egypt?

But look closely at what he has done. He has taken the failure of one situation and used it to predict the failure of the next. And he ends where he always ends — with his faltering lips.

We do this constantly. One rejection becomes proof that we will always be rejected. One failed attempt becomes evidence that we should never try again. Discouragement is a poor prophet, but we keep listening to it.

Notice that God had already addressed the speech problem in chapter 4, and Moses raises it again here. Old insecurities do not disappear after one conversation with God. They resurface, and they need answering again.

Do not be discouraged if a fear you thought you had settled comes back. God is patient with repeat wrestling. Keep bringing it to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What past failure am I using to predict a future one?
2. Which old insecurity keeps resurfacing that I need to bring to God again?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I keep returning to the same fears. Thank You for Your patience. Speak again to the insecurity I cannot seem to shake. Amen.
